title: Active learning found unconventional self-assembling pentapeptides
summary: An experiment-driven active-learning workflow selected pentapeptide sequences for testing of beta-sheet self-assembly. Among 268 synthesized and tested peptides, 96 formed beta-sheet assemblies, including sequences such as ILFSM, LMISI, MITIY, MISIW and WKIYI that conventional propensity rules did not predict. The result concerns measured assembly under the study conditions; it does not establish a functional material application or therapeutic effect. The outcome was already reported in the September 2024 preprint and is dated accordingly.
ai_technology: AI-driven active learning with machine-learning models that selected peptide sequences for iterative synthesis and testing
organization: Indian Institute of Technology Madras; Argonne National Laboratory; University of Illinois Chicago

source_review.scope: Primary PMC full article for active-learning workflow and measured assemblies; primary Research Square v1 manuscript for September 2024 version date and named affiliations; primary AAAS article for the peer-reviewed version and reported results.

evidence.tested: The v1 reports synthesis/testing of 268 pentapeptides and 96 beta-sheet-forming assemblies, including several unconventional sequences.
evidence.unknown: Assembly findings are bounded to the reported experimental conditions; no application-level performance, therapeutic efficacy or independent replication is established. The specific result was present in the preprint before journal publication.
evidence.ai_role: AI-driven active learning prioritized sequences for iterative synthesis and experimental characterization, focusing in part on cases where model predictions differed from conventional propensity tables.
